final:
Of the three review comments, two are wrong and one is partly right. Only the third needs a change, and it's a doc wording fix that can wait. I changed no code and posted no replies, and the verdicts are in `verdicts.json`.

| # | Category | Verdict | Change needed? |
|---|----------|---------|----------------|
| 0 | Correctness / compatibility | Invalid | No |
| 1 | Correctness | Invalid | No |
| 2 | Correctness (docs) | Partly valid | Optional |

**#0 – changing the "recreate" exit code from 4 to 3 breaks scripts.** It doesn't. Before this PR, the guide's exit-code table in `update-compatibility.adoc` already said 3 means "rolling upgrade not possible". Only the constant in the code was 4, so the PR makes the code match the docs. The command is still marked preview, isn't in any release notes, and the project version is a snapshot (`999.0.0-SNAPSHOT`). There was no released behaviour for scripts to depend on.

**#1 – picocli uses 3 for "usage error".** That's wrong. In picocli, 1 means software error and 2 means usage error; 3 has no meaning. The new comment at `CompatibilityResult.java:31-34` already lists 1 and 2 as picocli's, so the custom codes start at 3 to avoid them. I couldn't find the picocli jar locally, so this comes from picocli's documented constants rather than the jar itself.

**#2 – "Otherwise, the Operator will fail" is misleading.** The reviewer is right that the operator never checks the feature: nothing under `operator/src/main` references it. But their suggested replacement is wrong too, because in this PR the operator never runs the update-compatibility commands in pods. Only the tests turn the feature on. Without it, the commands fail only when someone runs them by hand. The note at `advanced-configuration.adoc:446-450` is probably written for a later version where the operator does run them. Rewording it would be a small, optional doc fix.
